title: Pre-Decision Three-Index Dispersion and Two-Book Relative Economic Value

research_height.transfer_path: Pre-decision internal index dispersion changes the opportunity set for US100 Cross/Passive relative to the directional US30 components, which can change book-level value and the evidence required for future portfolio allocation.

central_question: Does higher pre-decision cross-sectional dispersion among US100, US30 and US500 stably increase the fixed-0.01 stressed value of the US100 book relative to the US30 book, with the Cross component carrying the same direction?

research_bundle.name: predecision_dispersion_terciles_cross_mechanism_book_transfer_and_four_period_falsification
lenses: mechanism: Cross stressed net per lifecycle across outcome-free LOW, MID and HIGH three-index dispersion regimes
portfolio transfer: US100 minus US30 stressed net per lifecycle across the same regimes
breadth and falsification: repeat HIGH-minus-LOW direction in all four frozen periods while keeping Passive visible as a natural US100-book contrast

idea_provenance.authority_note: The memo supplies the economic question. Project Zeta Terminus Next remains the sole authority. The memo's weak n=4 period correlation is replaced before outcomes by a causal pre-decision daily regime with four-period breadth.

why_now.current_bottleneck: Unit 072 established two positive books with asymmetric protection, Unit 074 found unstable component frequency/value structure, and Unit 075 proved that the binding lifecycle distribution is incomplete. A complete CP2 population plus independent H1 market state can now test a concrete source of book-role variation without relying on the missing binding tail.
why_now.connection_bridge: Unit 064 found Cross common-variance share varied across periods and Unit 050 found large period variation in US30/US100 book economics. The immutable three-index H1 export and complete 2,233-lifecycle CP2 ledgers can join those facts at a strictly prior decision time.
why_now.perspective_distance: Unit 075 was Program 7 evidence-distribution reliability and failed before metrics. Unit 076 moves to Program 2 meso market-state mechanism with macro book transfer, uses bar returns as the treatment data role and a complete fixed-lot lifecycle population as outcomes.
why_now.decision_if_true: Keep both books and current construction, but classify their relative economic role as dispersion-dependent and retain one future, separately declared full-portfolio conditional-allocation seed; do not implement it here.
why_now.decision_if_false: Preserve the current unconditional two-book interpretation and discard three-index dispersion as a book-allocation context.
why_now.decision_if_ambiguous_or_invalid: Preserve current books and allocation, record the bounded result or observation gap and rotate away.

frozen_market_state.time_semantics: Use time_utc text exactly as the terminal-formatted server-time coordinate preserved by the source export; do not timezone-remap it.
frozen_market_state.h1_return: For each pair of consecutive physical H1 rows, calculate log(current open / prior open) separately for US100, US30 and US500.
frozen_market_state.interval_cross_sectional_dispersion: Population standard deviation of the three same-interval log returns around their equal-weight mean.
frozen_market_state.daily_score: At an exact server-calendar 12:00 H1 row, take the square root of the mean squared interval dispersion over the 24 consecutive physical H1 return intervals ending at that row.
frozen_market_state.causal_boundary: The exact 12:00 score precedes the earliest 12:15 decision. Do not use later same-day bars or lifecycle outcomes.
frozen_market_state.regime_thresholds: From all eligible H1 server dates, sort daily scores ascending. q1 is the value at one-based rank ceiling(N/3); q2 is the value at rank ceiling(2N/3). LOW is score <= q1, MID is q1 < score <= q2, HIGH is score > q2. Ties remain in the lower named regime.
frozen_market_state.lifecycle_assignment: Assign every reconstructed lifecycle the regime of its birth server-calendar date; exclude only dates without a frozen exact-12:00 score and report coverage.

frozen_lifecycle_reconstruction.ordering: Within each period concatenate its pinned files, then sort mapped birth/final rows by numeric state_sequence. Keys are period plus component plus monotonically assigned lifecycle ordinal.
frozen_lifecycle_reconstruction.birth: OPEN for RC16, RC4, Cross, Pressure and Return; PASSIVE_FILL for Passive.
frozen_lifecycle_reconstruction.final: CLOSE or EXTERNAL_CLOSE for every mapped component. value_b is stressed 2x lifecycle net.
frozen_lifecycle_reconstruction.pairing: Each component must alternate from no position to one birth and then one final event; pair that final event to the currently open birth. Any overlap, orphan final or unclosed birth invalidates the unit.
frozen_lifecycle_reconstruction.book_outcome: For each basis cell report lifecycle count, stressed net sum and mean stressed net per lifecycle. US100_RELATIVE_TO_US30 equals US100 mean minus US30 mean.
frozen_lifecycle_reconstruction.component_contrast: Report Cross and Passive separately under the same cells; only Cross carries the mechanism gate.

requirements: All ten byte/hash pins and source verdict/schema anchors pass.
The H1 export has exactly 24,417 unique strictly increasing rows and finite positive opens for all three indices.
Lifecycle reconstruction yields exactly 2,233 complete pairs, including 2,027 CLOSE and 206 EXTERNAL_CLOSE finals, with six counts and period/book stressed nets matching Unit 050 within 1e-9.
At least 95% of lifecycles in each period and each book map to an eligible exact-12:00 regime.
Each pooled book-by-regime cell has at least 100 mapped lifecycles; each period book-by-regime and Cross-by-regime cell has at least 15.
US100_RELATIVE_TO_US30 mean value is strictly ordered LOW < MID < HIGH.
HIGH minus LOW US100_RELATIVE_TO_US30 mean is at least +0.10 USD per lifecycle.
Cross HIGH minus LOW mean is at least +0.10 USD per lifecycle.
US100 book HIGH mean is strictly greater than its LOW mean.
HIGH minus LOW US100_RELATIVE_TO_US30 mean is positive in at least three of four periods.
Cross HIGH minus LOW mean is positive in at least three of four periods.

The dispersion thesis is strongly falsified when pooled HIGH-minus-LOW relative mean and pooled Cross HIGH-minus-LOW mean are both nonpositive, and each direction is positive in at most two of four periods.

fixed_verdict_rules.complete: PASS_THREE_INDEX_DISPERSION_CONDITIONS_TWO_BOOK_RELATIVE_VALUE when integrity, pooled dispersion and period breadth all pass.
fixed_verdict_rules.falsified: NO_THREE_INDEX_DISPERSION_BOOK_RELATIVE_VALUE_FIELD when integrity passes and the strong falsifier triggers.
fixed_verdict_rules.ambiguous: AMBIGUOUS_THREE_INDEX_DISPERSION_BOOK_RELATIVE_VALUE_NO_CANDIDATE when integrity passes and neither preceding rule applies.
fixed_verdict_rules.invalid: INVALID_THREE_INDEX_DISPERSION_BOOK_RELATIVE_VALUE_NO_VERDICT when any immutable, H1, lifecycle, coverage or density condition fails.

decision_translation.complete: Preserve both books and current allocation; retain one non-automatic future full-portfolio conditional-allocation seed that must separately test net, equity drawdown, fills and opportunity displacement.
decision_translation.falsified: Discard internal three-index dispersion as a book-allocation context and preserve unconditional book roles.
decision_translation.ambiguous_or_invalid: Make no book or allocation change and rotate away.

stop_rules: Commit and push declaration, state and Frontier memory before calculating any daily dispersion score, regime threshold or conditional book/component outcome.
One implementation-only correction is allowed only before any new dispersion or conditional outcome metric is emitted. After any new metric, make no correction or rerun.
Do not change the 12:00 boundary, 24-interval score, terciles, lifecycle events, books, thresholds, breadth, verdicts or decisions after outcomes.
Do not acquire data, create runtime, modify MQL, compile, run Tester, query broker/account state or touch Live.
